title: Timeline
description: A Content Fabrique edit: the declarative timeline (an EDL in JSON) that agents and users change through edit ops and that the Go compiler turns into one ffmpeg invocation. Every time is an integer number of milliseconds.
$comment: Structure only. The Go layer (apps/server/internal/timeline, docs/design/timeline-v1.md section 3) checks what a schema cannot: unique ids across the spec (duplicate_id), contiguity of the main track including the first item starting at 0 (gap, overlap), source ranges inside the asset, for video and audio, with in < out (source_out_of_range), output duration of an item >= 300 ms (shot_too_short), total duration 1 s to 180 s (duration_out_of_range), every text item, audio item and marker inside the total duration (outside_timeline), text inside the format safe zone (unsafe_text), asset ids that exist in the catalog (unknown_asset), transitions shorter than both items they join (transition_too_long), audio assets that are licensed or attested (unlicensed_audio), fades that fit the sound (fade_too_long), assets of the right kind (wrong_asset_kind), no transition on the first clip in time (first_transition) text styles that exist in the style registry (unknown_style), motion presets on clips of at least 400 ms with an at_ms inside the clip (invalid_motion), and speed ramps that are sorted, inside the source range and not combined with speed (invalid_speed_ramp; a ramp with use_source also raises the warning ramp_audio_muted). The schema is closed: no property is allowed outside the ones listed, at any level.

schema.title: Schema version
schema.description: The constant "contentfabrique.timeline/v1". It names the spec version the document follows.

tracks.title: Tracks
tracks.description: Exactly one video track (its id is "main"), at most one text track, at most one captions track, at most one audio track and at most one graphics track, in any order.

markers.title: Markers
markers.description: Beat grid and section marks that the editor uses to place cuts. They are never rendered.

ms.title: Milliseconds
ms.description: A time or duration as a whole number of milliseconds, from 0 to 86 400 000 (24 hours). No floats.

gainDb.title: Gain in dB
gainDb.description: Volume change in decibels, from -30 to +6. 0 leaves the level as it is.

itemId.title: Item id
itemId.description: A lowercase id of 1 to 32 characters: a letter, then letters, digits or underscores, such as "c1" or "t3". Ids are unique across the whole spec. The edit ops name items by these ids.

styleId.title: Style id
styleId.description: The id of a text style from the style registry, such as "title_bold". The spec can't name a font directly.

assetId.title: Asset id
assetId.description: TypeID of an asset: the prefix "ast_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

momentId.title: Moment id
momentId.description: TypeID of a moment: the prefix "mom_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

trendId.title: Trend id
trendId.description: TypeID of a trend: the prefix "trd_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

ideaId.title: Idea id
ideaId.description: TypeID of an idea: the prefix "ide_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

conceptId.title: Concept id
conceptId.description: TypeID of a concept: the prefix "con_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

licenseId.title: Licence id
licenseId.description: TypeID of a licence: the prefix "lic_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

output.title: Output
output.description: The rendered video: format, size, frame rate and background. The size must be the one of the format: 9:16 is 1080x1920, 1:1 is 1080x1080, 4:5 is 1080x1350 and 16:9 is 1920x1080.

format.title: Format
format.description: The aspect ratio the project was created with (D-25). It fixes the width and height.

height.title: Height
height.description: Height in pixels. 1920 for 9:16, 1080 for 1:1 and 16:9, 1350 for 4:5.

fps.title: Frame rate
fps.description: Frames per second of the render.

background.title: Background
background.description: Colour behind the video where nothing covers it (letterboxing in contain mode), as #rrggbb.

track.title: Track
track.description: A track, told apart by its "type": video, text, captions, audio or graphics.

videoTrack.title: Video track
videoTrack.description: The main track: the clips of the edit, one after the other. Items are sorted by at_ms, the first starts at 0 and has a cut, and each next one starts where the previous one ends (minus its own transition duration).

items.title: Clips
items.description: The clips in time order. The first clip must have a cut (or no transition_in). An empty list is structurally valid and fails the duration check.

videoItem.title: Video clip
videoItem.description: A cut from a source asset placed on the main track. Its output duration is floor((source.out_ms - source.in_ms) / speed + 0.5) ms.

source.title: Source range
source.description: The part of the asset to use, in the asset's own time. in_ms must be below out_ms and out_ms within the asset's duration (checked by the Go layer).

in_ms.title: In point
in_ms.description: Where the clip starts in the asset, in ms.

out_ms.title: Out point
out_ms.description: Where the clip ends in the asset, in ms. Exclusive.

at_ms.title: Start on the timeline
at_ms.description: When the clip starts in the output, in ms. It is redundant with the durations on purpose: the first clip is at 0 and each next one at the end of the previous one minus its own transition duration.

speed.title: Speed
speed.description: Playback speed from 0.25 (slow motion) to 4 (fast). Default 1. A clip has either speed or speed_ramp, not both (checked by the Go layer).

exposure_ev.title: Exposure hint
exposure_ev.description: A small nudge, -1 to 1 stops (EV): how much brighter this clip is than the exposure the edit should have (positive: too bright, to be darkened; negative: too dark, to be lifted). It must come from highlight or midtone percentiles of the clip, never from its mean brightness, because a low-key clip (black wall, lit subject) has a low mean and is correctly exposed. The renderer applies the opposite, limited to 0.7 stops and ignoring hints under 0.15, with a highlight-preserving curve that keeps the black point, when look.match is true or the preset is auto. Without it, nothing is corrected.

why.title: Why
why.description: Why the editor picked this clip, 280 characters at most. Shown to the creator in the UI and never rendered.

reframe.title: Reframe
reframe.description: How the source is fitted to the output frame. Without it, the clip uses cover, focus 0.5/0.5 and zoom 1.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: cover fills the frame and crops around the focus point. contain fits the whole source and pads with the background colour. blur_fill fits the whole source over a blurred, scaled copy of itself.

focus.title: Focus point
focus.description: The point of the source that the crop is centred on, as fractions of its width and height. Default 0.5/0.5. Only cover uses it.

x.title: Focus x
x.description: 0 is the left edge of the source, 1 the right edge.

y.title: Focus y
y.description: 0 is the top edge of the source, 1 the bottom edge.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Extra zoom into the centre of the framed clip, from 1 (none) to 3. Default 1.

speedRamp.title: Speed ramp
speedRamp.description: A speed that changes along the clip, as 2 to 16 points {at_ms, speed}. at_ms is a source offset: milliseconds into the clip's source range, counted from source.in_ms (0 to out_ms - in_ms), strictly increasing. The speed (0.25 to 4) changes linearly in source time between two points, is the first point's speed before the first and the last point's speed after the last. The clip's output duration is the integral of 1/speed over its source range. It replaces speed: give one of the two. The clip's own audio is muted (it cannot follow the ramp). Sorted points and the range are checked by the Go layer.

at_ms.title: Source offset
at_ms.description: Where the point is, in ms from source.in_ms (in source time).

speed.title: Speed
speed.description: The playback speed at the point, 0.25 to 4.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: A camera move on the clip, applied as a digital zoom on the already-reframed frame (after reframe, so it composes with every reframe mode and never shows a border). punch_in is a fast zoom (about 5 frames) that lands at at_ms and holds, push_in a slow continuous zoom over the whole clip, pull_back the reverse (starts zoomed, pulls back to the full frame), shake a short camera shake that starts at at_ms and dies out (deterministic: the pattern comes from the clip's id), and handheld the living camera of a tripod shot: a slow push over the whole clip, a gentle drift that alternates direction from one clip to the next and a slow sway, so the shot never sits dead still, with a punch-in of 6 % that lands at at_ms when it is given (the drop or a strong beat); the renderer keeps the push off the subject's head and body when the clip has a subject box. Needs a clip of at least 400 ms (checked by the Go layer).

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: none, punch_in, push_in, pull_back, shake or handheld.

at_ms.title: At
at_ms.description: Only for punch_in (where the zoom has landed), shake (where it starts) and handheld (where its punch-in lands): milliseconds from the clip's first frame, inside the clip. Without it punch_in zooms over the first frames of the clip, shake starts at its first frame and handheld has no punch-in.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: The peak scale increase, 0.05 (5 % bigger) to 0.35. Defaults: punch_in 0.15, push_in 0.1, pull_back 0.15, shake 0.08 (also the size of the shake), handheld 0.08 (the push over the clip).

look.title: Look
look.description: A colour treatment for the clip. Without it, the clip has no treatment.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: A fixed colour preset: none, punchy (more contrast and saturation), warm, cool, bw (black and white), matte (lifted blacks), auto (a mild contrast curve that keeps blacks and whites where they are, plus the clip's exposure_ev nudge, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure without washing out low-key footage) or gym_moody (warm skin, a little contrast above the shadows, a soft vignette; dark shadows are left alone).

match.title: Match exposure
match.description: True to correct the clip's exposure by its exposure_ev hint (from the analysis; a nudge of at most 0.7 stops, black point kept) before the preset, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure. The preset auto always does this, whatever match says. Default false. Without an exposure_ev on the clip it changes nothing.

transition.title: Transition in
transition.description: How the clip begins. A cut is instant. The other types blend with the previous clip over duration_ms, and the clip then starts that long before the previous one ends. The first clip must have a cut.

type.title: Type
type.description: crossfade blends the two clips. dip_to_black fades out to black and in again. whip_left is a fast slide to the left with motion blur (whip is the same, kept for older edits); whip_right slides to the right. zoom_through zooms into the outgoing clip and out of the incoming one through a blur. flash dips to white. punch is a fast scale of 1.0 to 1.15 into the cut through a blur, settling on the incoming clip: a hit for a strong beat. The whips, zoom_through and punch ride a motion-blur trail that peaks at the middle of the transition, where the picture switches; the frames before and after it are sharp.

duration_ms.title: Duration
duration_ms.description: Length of the transition in ms, 100 to 1000. It must be shorter than both clips it joins (checked by the Go layer).

videoAudio.title: Clip audio
videoAudio.description: What the clip's own sound does: mode mute, bed or full (or the old use_source). Without it, the clip is silent.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: What the clip's own sound does. mute: nothing (the default: a clip with no audio settings is silent). bed: a low ambience under the edit, evened out across the clips and never normalised up to the programme, so the export is not silent where no sound is playing and the creator can add a trend sound on top; use it for footage with no speech (gym clatter, room tone). full: the programme: the clip's sound at its own level, normalised with the rest and ducked under sound effects; use it for speech. gain_db is a trim on top of the mode's level.

use_source.title: Use source audio
use_source.description: The old spelling of mode: true is full, false is mute. Not together with mode.

gain_db.title: Gain
gain_db.description: Volume change of the clip's audio in dB, from -30 to +6. Default 0.

textTrack.title: Text track
textTrack.description: Titles and captions that are written by hand. They are rendered as styled, animated text. At most one text track.

id.title: Track id
id.description: The track's id, such as "text". Unique across the whole spec.

items.title: Text items
items.description: The text items. They may overlap each other and may sit anywhere inside the total duration.

textItem.title: Text item
textItem.description: A piece of text shown for a while. Give it exactly one of anchor or position.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the text appears, in ms. Text keeps its absolute time when clips move.

duration_ms.title: Duration
duration_ms.description: How long the text stays, in ms. At least 300. It must end inside the total duration (checked by the Go layer).

text.title: Text
text.description: The words to show: 1 to 120 characters and at most 3 lines. Lines are separated by a newline (\n). No other control character is allowed, and neither are the line and paragraph separators U+2028 and U+2029.

anchor.title: Anchor
anchor.description: A safe place for the text: upper_third, center or lower_third. Set this or position, not both.

position.title: Position
position.description: A free place for the text's centre as fractions of the frame. The text must stay inside the format's safe zone (checked by the Go layer). Set this or anchor, not both.

x.title: Position x
x.description: 0 is the left edge of the frame, 1 the right edge.

y.title: Position y
y.description: 0 is the top edge of the frame, 1 the bottom edge.

animation.title: Animation
animation.description: How the text enters: none, pop_in, fade, typewriter, slide_up or pop (scales up past its size and settles back, with a fade: the lively entrance). Default none.

exit.title: Exit
exit.description: How the text leaves at its end: none (it is cut), fade, pop_out (shrinks away with a fade) or slide_down (sinks a little with a fade). Default none.

fill.title: Fill colour
fill.description: The colour of the letters as #RRGGBB, for this text only (for example #F2E9A0). Without it the style's own colour is used.

scale.title: Size scale
scale.description: The size of the text relative to its style's size, from 0.6 to 1.4 (kept to a hundredth). Without it the style's own size (1) is used.

shadow.title: Shadow
shadow.description: The drop shadow of the letters: none, soft (a light one) or strong (a heavy one). Without it the style's own shadow is used.

align.title: Alignment
align.description: How the lines of a text of more than one line sit against each other in its box: left, center or right. Default center.

avoid_subject.title: Avoid the subject
avoid_subject.description: Whether the renderer keeps this text off the head of the person in the footage: when it would cover the head it is moved above or below it inside the safe zone, or shrunk within the allowed scale. true by default; set false to place the text exactly where its anchor or position puts it.

graphicsTrack.title: Graphics track
graphicsTrack.description: Motion-graphics overlays (templates with params), drawn over the video under the text and captions. At most one graphics track.

id.title: Track id
id.description: The track's id, such as "graphics". Unique across the whole spec.

items.title: Graphics items
items.description: The overlays, at most 64. They may overlap each other in time and sit anywhere inside the total duration; the renderer keeps two on screen at once apart in the frame.

graphicsItem.title: Graphics item
graphicsItem.description: A motion-graphics overlay: a template from the library with its params, rendered as animated frames over the video (an animated title, a chapter card, a counter, a label). Give it exactly one of anchor or position. Its box is laid out like a text item's and kept inside the safe zone and off the subject.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the overlay starts to enter, in ms. It keeps its absolute time when clips move.

duration_ms.title: Duration
duration_ms.description: How long the overlay is on screen, entrance and exit included, in ms. At least 500; give it room to be read (about 1.2 s after its entrance).

anchor.title: Anchor
anchor.description: A safe place for the text: upper_third, center or lower_third. Set this or position, not both.

position.title: Position
position.description: A free place for the text's centre as fractions of the frame. The text must stay inside the format's safe zone (checked by the Go layer). Set this or anchor, not both.

x.title: Position x
x.description: 0 is the left edge of the frame, 1 the right edge.

y.title: Position y
y.description: 0 is the top edge of the frame, 1 the bottom edge.

avoid_subject.title: Avoid the subject
avoid_subject.description: Whether the renderer keeps this text off the head of the person in the footage: when it would cover the head it is moved above or below it inside the safe zone, or shrunk within the allowed scale. true by default; set false to place the text exactly where its anchor or position puts it.

params.title: Params
params.description: The template's params; which fields are allowed depends on the template.

graphicsTemplate.title: Template
graphicsTemplate.description: The motion-graphics template the item uses (docs/design/motion-graphics-v1.md). title_pop: word by word: each word scales up with a blur and an overshoot, landing on its accent (a beat); for a hook title; blur_in: the title sharpens out of a blur while it drifts into place; a quieter title; chapter_card: a numbered chapter title: the number pops first in the accent colour, then the line sweeps in after it; one or two lines; highlight_word: a line where one word gets a marker swiped in behind it in the accent colour; counter: a number that counts from one value to another and lands with a pop, followed by its label (12 REPS, 100 KG); lower_label: a small label on a plate with an accent stripe that slides in; for a name, an exercise or a tag; outro_card: the loop card at the end: letters drop in, an accent line grows under them, and it pushes out on the last frame.

graphicsParam.title: Graphics params
graphicsParam.description: The params a graphics template may take. Each template's own definition lists which of them it allows.

text.title: Text
text.description: The words: 1 to 60 characters, at most 2 lines (separated by \n). For counter it is the label after the number (REPS, KG); for chapter_card the chapter's title without its number. Set as plain text, never markup.

style.description: The text style from the style registry: it picks the font, size, colour and shadow (the creator's title style, such as title_series). Default: title_bold, or label_box for lower_label and stat_big for counter.

fill.title: Fill colour
fill.description: The colour of the letters as #RRGGBB. Without it the style's own colour is used.

accent.title: Accent colour
accent.description: The accent colour as #RRGGBB: the chapter number, the marker, the label stripe, the outro line. Default #FFD60A.

scale.title: Size scale
scale.description: The size relative to the style's, 0.6 to 1.4. Default 1.

align.title: Alignment
align.description: How the lines sit against each other in the box. Default center.

shadow.title: Shadow
shadow.description: The drop shadow of the letters. Without it the style's own.

backing.title: Backing
backing.description: plate puts a translucent dark plate behind the text, for legibility over a busy or bright picture. Default none.

energy.title: Energy
energy.description: How hard the motion hits: calm (slow, soft, no overshoot to speak of), lively (the default) or hype (fast stagger, a bigger overshoot and blur). Match the vibe of the edit.

accents_ms.title: Accents
accents_ms.description: Timeline times (ms, like markers) the motion lands on, strictly increasing and inside the item: usually beats. title_pop lands word i on accent i and pulses on the rest; chapter_card pops the number on the first and sweeps the line on the second; highlight_word swipes the marker on the first; counter lands the count on the first; lower_label and outro_card enter on the first. Without accents the template uses its own stagger.

number.title: Chapter number
number.description: The chapter's number, written as "1." before the title.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: one_line puts the number before the title; two_line puts it on a line of its own above.

word.title: Highlighted word
word.description: Which word gets the marker, counting from 1 across the lines.

from.title: From
from.description: The value the counter starts at.

to.title: To
to.description: The value the counter lands on.

decimals.title: Decimals
decimals.description: Digits after the decimal point, 0 to 2. Default 0.

graphicsParamsTitlePop.title: title_pop params
graphicsParamsTitlePop.description: The params of a title_pop item: word by word: each word scales up with a blur and an overshoot, landing on its accent (a beat); for a hook title.

graphicsParamsBlurIn.title: blur_in params
graphicsParamsBlurIn.description: The params of a blur_in item: the title sharpens out of a blur while it drifts into place; a quieter title.

graphicsParamsChapterCard.title: chapter_card params
graphicsParamsChapterCard.description: The params of a chapter_card item: a numbered chapter title: the number pops first in the accent colour, then the line sweeps in after it; one or two lines.

graphicsParamsHighlightWord.title: highlight_word params
graphicsParamsHighlightWord.description: The params of a highlight_word item: a line where one word gets a marker swiped in behind it in the accent colour.

graphicsParamsCounter.title: counter params
graphicsParamsCounter.description: The params of a counter item: a number that counts from one value to another and lands with a pop, followed by its label (12 REPS, 100 KG).

graphicsParamsLowerLabel.title: lower_label params
graphicsParamsLowerLabel.description: The params of a lower_label item: a small label on a plate with an accent stripe that slides in; for a name, an exercise or a tag.

graphicsParamsOutroCard.title: outro_card params
graphicsParamsOutroCard.description: The params of a outro_card item: the loop card at the end: letters drop in, an accent line grows under them, and it pushes out on the last frame.

captionsTrack.title: Captions track
captionsTrack.description: Captions made from the transcript's word timestamps. It holds settings, not items. At most one captions track.

id.title: Track id
id.description: The track's id, such as "captions". Unique across the whole spec.

from.title: Source
from.description: "transcript": the words come from the transcript of the clips' audio.

style.title: Style
style.description: word_highlight shows a few words and highlights the one being said. chunk shows each group of words at once.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: True to render the captions. False keeps the settings without rendering them.

uppercase.title: Uppercase
uppercase.description: True to write the captions in capitals. Default true.

max_words.title: Maximum words
max_words.description: The most words on screen at once, 1 to 4. Default 2.

audioTrack.title: Audio track
audioTrack.description: Music and sound on top of the clips' own audio. Items may overlap, because they are mixed. At most one audio track.

id.title: Track id
id.description: The track's id, such as "sound". Unique across the whole spec.

audioItem.title: Audio item
audioItem.description: A sound in the mix, told apart by its "kind": trend_sound (cue-only, never reproduced by us), licensed_track (from the licensed library), creator_audio (the creator's own upload) or sfx (a sound effect the renderer synthesises: no asset, always in the export).

trendSound.title: Trend sound
trendSound.description: A trending sound. It is a cue for the creator to add the sound in TikTok and is never mixed or exported by us (D-03), so its export must be "cue_only". Previews play a generated beat guide instead.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the sound starts in the output, in ms.

source_offset_ms.title: Source offset
source_offset_ms.description: Where in the sound to start playing, in ms.

export.title: Export policy
export.description: Always "cue_only" for a trend sound: it is never reproduced by us.

licensedTrack.title: Licensed track
licensedTrack.description: A track from the licensed library. It is mixed into the render, so its export must be "licensed".

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the track starts in the output, in ms.

source_offset_ms.title: Source offset
source_offset_ms.description: Where in the track to start playing, in ms.

export.title: Export policy
export.description: Always "licensed": the track is mixed into the render.

sfxName.title: Effect
sfxName.description: The effect category: whoosh, swish, impact, riser, downlifter, sub_drop, pop, click, glitch, shimmer, sting.

sfxVariant.title: Variant
sfxVariant.description: Optional variant of the effect, one of the variants of its category: whoosh: air, fast, heavy; swish: thin, blade, cloth; impact: punch, deep, crack, metal; riser: tension, sweep, pitch, long; downlifter: fall, short, tape; sub_drop: boom, quick, long; pop: bubble, tick, double; click: ui, soft, tonal, mech; glitch: stutter, crush, chirp; shimmer: sparkle, wash, rise; sting: hit, bright, dark. Without it the category's first variant is used, which is what the effects were before variants existed. "auto" picks one of the category's variants from a hash of the item id, so repeats of one effect differ. Every item also gets a small, deterministic jitter of pitch, length and filter from its id, so two items of the same variant are never exactly the same sample.

sfxSound.title: Sound effect
sfxSound.description: A sound effect that the renderer synthesises itself (no asset, no licence: it is ours, so its export is "licensed" and it is in every render and export). Each effect is built from layers (a transient, a body, a sub with a pitch drop, air or tail), banded, lightly saturated, glued by a compressor and given a short dark room, then loudness-matched to its category. Categories: whoosh (an air pass-by for a whip or a cut; variants air 0.6 s, fast 0.35 s, heavy 1.0 s with weight), swish (a quick thin air pass for small moves; thin 0.3 s, blade 0.2 s, cloth 0.4 s), impact (a low hit with a crack for a punch-in or the drop; punch 0.8 s, deep 1.4 s with a long sub, crack 0.5 s bright, metal 1.2 s), riser (a rising tension build that peaks at its end, so start it that long before the moment it leads to; tension 1.5 s, sweep 1.0 s filter sweep, pitch 2.0 s tonal, long 3.0 s), downlifter (a falling release after a hit or on the new section; fall 1.2 s, short 0.6 s, tape 0.8 s tape stop), sub_drop (a pitch-dropping sine under a hit; boom 1.0 s, quick 0.5 s, long 2.0 s), pop (a small bubble for an element appearing; bubble 0.3 s, tick 0.15 s, double 0.35 s), click (a UI click on the frame of an on-screen press; ui 80 ms, soft 100 ms, tonal 120 ms, mech 180 ms), glitch (a digital stutter for a glitchy cut; stutter 0.3 s, crush 0.25 s, chirp 0.4 s), shimmer (a sparkle for something magical or new; sparkle 1.2 s, wash 1.5 s, rise 1.0 s), sting (a logo or reveal hit with a tonal bloom; hit 2.5 s, bright 2.0 s, dark 3.0 s). It starts at at_ms and is cut at the end of the timeline. It is mixed at a fixed level plus gain_db, so it stays an accent. With speech (a clip in mode full) it is mixed after the loudness normalisation, above the programme, and the programme is ducked a few dB around it; with no speech (clips in mode bed or mute) it is mixed over the bed, which is not normalised (about -24 LUFS), with the effect lifted a few dB so that it peaks around -12 to -10 LUFS and cuts through a trend sound at -14.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the effect starts in the output, in ms. For an impact or a riser that should land on a beat, start it before the beat by the time it takes to build: a riser ends as long after it starts as its variant is long (1500 ms for the default).

export.title: Export policy
export.description: Always "licensed": the effect is ours and is mixed into the render.

creatorAudio.title: Creator audio
creatorAudio.description: Audio the creator uploaded themselves, with a rights attestation. It is mixed into the render, so its export must be "licensed".

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the audio starts in the output, in ms.

source_offset_ms.title: Source offset
source_offset_ms.description: Where in the audio to start playing, in ms.

export.title: Export policy
export.description: Always "licensed": the audio is mixed into the render.

audioDuration.title: Duration
audioDuration.description: How long the sound plays, in ms, 1 or more. Without it, it plays to the end of the timeline. The sound must end inside the total duration, and source_offset_ms + this duration must fit inside the asset (both checked by the Go layer).

fadeIn.title: Fade in
fadeIn.description: Length of the fade in at the start, in ms. Without it, there is no fade. fade_in_ms + fade_out_ms must not exceed the sound's duration (checked by the Go layer).

fadeOut.title: Fade out
fadeOut.description: Length of the fade out at the end, in ms. Without it, there is no fade. fade_in_ms + fade_out_ms must not exceed the sound's duration (checked by the Go layer).

marker.title: Marker
marker.description: A point on the beat grid or a section boundary, in output time.

at_ms.title: Time
at_ms.description: Where the marker is in the output, in ms. It must be inside the total duration (checked by the Go layer).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: beat is a beat of the bar, downbeat the first beat of a bar, drop the big moment of the track and section the start of a part.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: How strong the marker is, from 0 to 1. Default 1.

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Links back to the idea and concept this edit was made for.
